item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J00715","case1_error":"Counts Reece’s 26-foot ladder only once, omitting his 15 climbs.","case2_error":"Returns 95 total knockouts instead of first-round knockouts, despite writing the correct first-round formula.","reason":"The first omits a repetition factor; the second answers with the intermediate quantity rather than the requested subset.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00716","case1_error":"Assigns two legs to each of the other walker’s dogs instead of four, then rounds the resulting fractional count.","case2_error":"Uses three planks per leg despite the stated requirement of one plank per leg.","reason":"Both construct their totals using an incorrect per-unit count that contradicts the stated or acknowledged count.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J00717","case1_error":"Omits the $20 flat fee from the total deposit.","case2_error":"Omits the 15 retained cards when calculating how many cards Miguel received.","reason":"Both omit a required fixed component from the accounting relation; the differing addition and subtraction do not change the mechanism.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J00718","case1_error":"Evaluates the correctly written sum 30 + 35 + 46 as 101 instead of 111.","case2_error":"Evaluates the existing decorations as 55 instead of 53 and omits the 10 decorations remaining to put up.","reason":"The first is solely an arithmetic evaluation error. The second also drops a required component from the final total.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J00719","case1_error":"Treats each smaller antacid as weighing three grams instead of one gram, producing nine grams for three pills.","case2_error":"Treats the $2 price for five cans as the price per can.","reason":"Both assign an inflated amount to each individual unit before multiplying by the item count; their subsequent arithmetic follows that incorrect assignment.","judgment":"same"}]}
